Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

general adjective

common to all, not particular

also common to all, universal, the general good, common (shared), in common, have in common

classical

Ov. Met. 6.349: ūsus commūnis aquārum est
Cic. Sest. 15: commūnis salūs (Lewis & Short)

commūnis, commūne

adjective, third declension

common to all, general, shared

The opposite is proprius, one’s own (Quint. 7.3.24, Lewis & Short). The general good is commūnis ūtilitās (Gell. 12.1.24).

Other words

  • ūniversus, ūniversa, ūniversum — of all together, of the whole

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.26: ūtilitās ūnīus cujusque et ūniversōrum; Liv. 22.32.2: ūniversa dīmicātiō, a general engagement (Lewis & Short)

    All taken together, as against each one (singulī).

  • generālis, generāle — general (as against particular); of a kind

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.96: generāle quoddam decōrum (Lewis & Short); Quint. 12.2.18 (Lewis & Short)

    A word of philosophy and rhetoric, opposed to speciālis; rare before Augustus, frequent in Quintilian and Seneca (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quid prohibētis aquīs? ūsus commūnis aquārum est. nec sōlem proprium nātūra nec āëra fēcit nec tenuēs undās: ad pūblica mūnera vēnī

    Why keep me from the water? Water is for everyone to use. Nature made neither the sun nor the air nor the clear water anyone’s own: I have come to gifts that belong to all.Ov. Met. 6.349–351

  • Ergō ūnum dēbet esse omnibus prōpositum, ut eadem sit ūtilitās ūnīus cujusque et ūniversōrum

    So everyone should have one aim: that the good of each and the good of all should be the sameCic. Off. 3.26

  • vetus verbum hoc quidem est: commūnia esse amīcōrum inter sē omnia

    it is an old saying, this: friends have everything in commonTer. Ad. 803–804

See also in general, special, particular, common.
